rubric.why: Physiology is defined by the study of functions in living organisms.
rubric.description: Defines physiology as the study of functions of living organisms or their parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the study of functions as physiology’s subject; accept a clear equivalent definition.

rubric.why: Taxonomy deals with identifying, naming and classifying organisms.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomy as the branch of biology concerned with identifying, naming and classifying organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking taxonomy with classification and at least one of identification or naming.

modelAnswer: Physiology is the branch of biology that deals with the functions of living organisms and their parts.
Taxonomy is the branch of biology concerned with the identification, naming and classification of organisms.

rubric.why: Horticulture is defined by the cultivation of garden crops.
rubric.description: Defines horticulture as the cultivation of garden crops such as fruits, vegetables or ornamental plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying cultivation of garden crops or giving suitable examples.

rubric.why: Horticulture is a specialized branch of agriculture.
rubric.description: States how horticulture is related to agriculture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that horticulture is a branch or specialized part of agriculture.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is the branch of agriculture concerned with cultivating garden crops, such as fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
It is related to agriculture because it is a specialized part of agriculture.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a hypothesis and a theory.

rubric.why: A scientific law describes a consistent pattern or what happens.
rubric.description: Explains that a law describes what happens or states a consistent pattern in nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the descriptive role of a law.

rubric.why: A scientific theory explains why or how natural events occur.
rubric.description: Explains that a theory gives an explanation for natural events.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the explanatory role of a theory.

modelAnswer: A law describes a consistent pattern in nature or states what happens.
A theory explains why or how that pattern or event occurs.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell membrane.

rubric.why: The membrane’s basic framework is a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.description: Identifies the phospholipid bilayer as the basic structure of the membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the phospholipid bilayer or two phospholipid layers.

rubric.why: Proteins embedded in the bilayer give the membrane its mosaic appearance; their movement contributes to its fluid nature.
rubric.description: Mentions proteins embedded in or associated with the bilayer and links the model to fluidity or a mosaic arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying membrane proteins and the fluid/mosaic arrangement.

modelAnswer: The fluid mosaic model describes the cell membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
The lipids and some proteins can move within the membrane, making it fluid; the scattered proteins give it a mosaic appearance.

items.followUp: What is endocytosis? Give one function.

rubric.why: Exocytosis occurs when an intracellular vesicle joins the plasma membrane.
rubric.description: Defines exocytosis as the fusion of a vesicle with the plasma membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing vesicle fusion with the cell membrane.

rubric.why: Fusion releases vesicle contents outside the cell, enabling secretion or waste removal.
rubric.description: Gives the outward release of cell contents and/or a valid importance such as secretion or waste removal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that substances are released outside the cell or giving a valid function.

modelAnswer: Exocytosis is the process in which a vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane and releases its contents outside the cell.
It is important for secretion of substances and removal of wastes from the cell.

items.followUp: State two advantages of classifying organisms.

rubric.why: Grouping organisms makes their study more manageable.
rubric.description: States that classification organizes organisms into groups and makes their study easier.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning organized grouping or easier study.

rubric.why: Classification helps identify organisms and understand similarities, differences or relationships among them.
rubric.description: States that classification helps with identification or shows relationships/similarities and differences.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid additional aim of classification.

modelAnswer: Classification arranges organisms into groups, making them easier to study.
It helps in identifying organisms and understanding their similarities, differences and relationships.

items.followUp: What are unicellular organisms? Give one example.

rubric.why: The defining feature is that the organism is made of many cells.
rubric.description: States that simple multicellular organisms consist of many cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their multicellular nature.

rubric.why: In simple multicellular organisms, cells are not organized into true tissues; sponges are an example.
rubric.description: States that their cells lack tissue-level organization, or gives a suitable example such as a sponge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the lack of true tissues or a suitable example.

modelAnswer: Simple multicellular organisms are made of many cells, but their cells are not organized into true tissues.

items.followUp: What is the cell plate, and how does it form in a plant cell?

rubric.why: The phragmoplast develops between the daughter nuclei during plant-cell division, from spindle remnants and associated microtubules.
rubric.description: Identifies the phragmoplast as a structure formed between daughter nuclei from spindle microtubules or remnants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its position and/or formation from spindle microtubules.

rubric.why: The phragmoplast guides the formation of the cell plate, which separates the daughter cells.
rubric.description: States that the phragmoplast guides or helps form the cell plate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the phragmoplast to cell-plate formation.

modelAnswer: During telophase of plant-cell division, spindle microtubules between the daughter nuclei form the phragmoplast.
The phragmoplast guides Golgi-derived vesicles to the centre of the cell, where they fuse to form the cell plate.
